                      ORDER SUSPENDING ADVICE NOTICE NO. 317

        THIS MATTER comes before the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) upon El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE”) Application for Revision of its Retail

Electric Rates Pursuant to Advice Notice No. 317 (“Application”). Accompanying the Application,

EPE filed Advice Notice No. 317, which incorporates the requests included in the Application.

        The Commission finds that a hearing should be held concerning the reasonableness of the

proposed rates and, accordingly, suspends the operation of Advice Notice No. 317 for an initial

period of nine-months. 1

                                          BACKGROUND 2

        1.      On March 27, 2026, EPE filed its Application, requesting authority to change its

base rates. Specifically, among other assertions, EPE states its cost of service demonstrates a $70.6

million non-fuel base rate revenue deficiency, reflecting a 50.4 percent non-fuel base rate

increase. 3 EPE requests a net revenue increase of $70.4 million and a weighted average cost of

          2.    EPE asserts the non-fuel base rate increase is required to recover costs for EPE’s

investments of $2.4 billion on a total company basis and $408.44 million for New Mexico since

EPE’s last rate case, filed in 2020, 7 for new electric plant(s) in service and used to serve EPE’s

customers. 8 EPE asserts the relevant investments for New Mexico include $197.34 million in

distribution plant(s), $55.59 million in transmission plant(s), $28.86 million in nuclear production

plant(s), $66.8 million for local general plant(s), and $59.85 million in general plant(s). 9

          3.    Among other proposals, EPE proposes to include in base rates its Commission-

approved advanced meter system program costs 10 and annual capacity costs associated with

Commission-approved agreements for three battery energy storage facilities. 11

          4.    EPE states it exceeded $1.2 million per year in charitable donations since its last

rate case, and has not requested any amount of charitable donations in base rates. 12 EPE proposes

the base rates also include $4.75 million in costs related to apprenticeship programs for technical

and professional positions for students in local high schools and colleges, $138.5 million in costs

related to supplier diversity, and less than $100,000 in costs related to entry-level training

programs. 13

           5.     EPE asserts that it has made significant capital investments critical to the

modernization and reliability of its system to address complex challenges, including: load growth

and electrification, transition to cleaner energy resources, grid modernization, reliability,

resilience, and extreme weather. 14 EPE states that these investments and inflationary pressures are

the primary drivers behind the increase in costs for EPE to dependably serve its customers. 15

          6.     For these reasons, EPE states it intends to demonstrate that:

                 a. its currently authorized rates are no longer just and reasonable, will
                    not adequately attract and encourage investment of capital if left
                    unchanged, and do not allow for reasonable return on investment in
                    public utility plant(s) and property;

                 b. its rates and authorized revenues as presently allocated do not
                    adequately reflect the cost of service for the respective classes of
                    electric customers; and

                 c. the rates proposed in Advice Notice No. 317, which was concurrently
                    filed with the Application, are just and reasonable and should be
                    approved. 16

          7.     EPE further states it recognizes the significance in a $70.6 million base rate

deficiency, representing a 50.4 percent increase in base rate revenues. 17 To moderate the rate

impact, EPE proposes to phase in recovery through a two-part implementation of base rates for

Residential, Irrigation, Military, Private Lightning, Outdoor Lightning, and State University

customer classes. 18 EPE proposes the first phase, expected to take effect on January 1, 2027,

represents a system average increase of 26.8 percent, and the second phase, proposed to take place

on October 1, 2027, represents an additional 18.6 percent increase. 19 EPE asserts it does not intend

          8.      EPE asserts its Application is based on a twelve-month base period ending on

September 30, 2025 for the test year consistent with the provisions set forth in NMSA 1978,

Section 62-6-14(D). 21

          9.      The Application includes requests for several other approvals, summarized in the

4,157-page filing and in the attached testimonies of EPE’s witnesses. Additionally, accompanying

the Application is Advice Notice No. 317 and associated rate schedules. The proposed rates in

Advice Notice No. 317 have an effective date of May 1, 2026. 22

          10.     On April 2, 2026, the Commission issued its Order Appointing Co-Hearing

Examiners 23 to preside over this matter. 24

          11.     On April 15, 2026, EPE filed a Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits

(“Notice of Errata”). In the Notice of Errata, EPE stated it discovered or was made aware that there

were several errors in its initial Application filing. 25 Specifically, the errors included: a wrong

document filed, incorrect formatting, and, most significantly, missing workpapers. 26 EPE

requested the corrected pages attached to its Notice of Errata, which amounted to over 1,600 pages,

are substituted for the incorrect versions filed with EPE’s Application. 27

                                                 DISCUSSION

         12.     An application proposing new rates must conform to the requirements set forth in

Rule 17.1.210 NMAC (“Rule 210”), which applies to utility applications for new rates. When

typographical errors are made in an application, Rule 210 requires utilities to file corrected pages

with the Commission and include a letter of explanation before the application may be deemed

complete. 28 Further, applications which do not meet the requirements of Rule 210 shall not be

deemed complete. 29 If an application is found to be incomplete, the Commission shall advise the

utility of the deficiencies within 30 days of the filing and hold the Rates, Rules, or Forms for a

reasonable time until the required additional information or necessary corrections are provided. 30

If an application is found to be “significantly incomplete,” then the Commission may dismiss the

application. 31 No statutory deadline shall begin until the application is deemed complete by the

Commission. 32

         13.     No utility shall make changes to any rate, except after 30 days’ notice to the

Commission, and which shall plainly state the changes proposed to be made. 33 The utility shall

also provide when the changes to the rates will go into effect and provide other information as the

Commission’s rules require. 34

          14.     When a complete application proposing new rates is filed with the Commission,

the Commission may hold a hearing concerning the reasonableness of the proposed rates. 35 If the

Commission deems it necessary to assess the reasonableness of a proposed rate, the Commission

shall suspend the operation of the proposed rate before the rates become effective for an initial

period of nine months. 36 The Commission may extend the period for an additional three months if

deemed necessary. 37

         15.     In this matter, EPE must conform with the requirements set forth in Rule 210, which

requires an application proposing new rates to be complete before the Commission will accept it.

EPE’s Notice of Errata demonstrates that there were significant deficiencies in EPE’s initial

Application, making the initial Application incomplete. Specifically, EPE’s initial Application did

not include several workpapers, which are required to be provided in support of rate schedules for

investor-owned electric utilities.38 Additionally, EPE’s Notice of Errata is 1657 pages, which is

nearly 40 percent of the pages attached to EPE’s initial Application. Given that the initial

Application was missing required information established by the Commission’s Rules, and due to

the sheer breadth of the Notice of Errata, the deficiencies are significant.

         16.     The significant deficiencies were corrected, however, when EPE filed its Notice of

Errata on April 15, 2026. For this reason, the Application is deemed complete as of April 15,

2026. 39 The Commission will consider the 30 days’ notice of the proposed change in rates required

“significantly incomplete,” see Docket No. 16-00269-UT, Final Order, the Commission finds it is not necessary
to do so here because EPE cured the significant deficiencies when it filed the Notice of Errata. Administrative
efficiency would not be served by requiring EPE to re-file the Application entirely.

 to be given to the Commission under NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(B) to begin on April 15, 2026

as well. Additionally, no parties are prejudiced because the start of the suspension period is only

extended by two weeks.

       17.     Moreover, given the breadth of the Application, the additional documentation

provided in the Notice of Errata, and the implications the Application will have on New Mexico

ratepayers, a hearing is necessary to assess the reasonableness of the proposed rates.

       18.     Accordingly, Advice Notice No. 317 should be suspended for an initial period of

nine months beginning 30 days after the Commission was properly notified of the proposed rate

changes and the date EPE’s Application was considered complete. The Commission may later

extend the period of suspension for an additional three months if the Commission deems such an

extension to be necessary.

                               FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS

       The Commission finds and concludes:

       19.     The Commission was properly notified of the proposed rate changes, and the

Application is deemed complete as of April 15, 2026.

       20.     A hearing is necessary to assess the reasonableness of the proposed rates.

       21.     Advice Notice No. 317 should be suspended to hold said hearing beginning 30 days

after the Commission was properly notified of the proposed rate changes and the date EPE’s

Application was considered complete, which falls on May 15, 2026, for an initial period of nine

months.

       22.     The Commission may extend the suspension period for an additional three months

if the Commission determines that a longer period of time will be required to resolve this matter.

        IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       A.      The proposed rates filed by EPE in Advice Notice No. 317 are suspended for an

initial period of nine months, commencing on May 15, 2026.

       B.      The Commission may extend the suspension period, up to an additional three

months, should it determine more time is necessary to resolve this matter.

       C.      This Order is effective when signed.

       D.      In computing time in accordance with statute, regulation, or Commission order, the

computation shall begin on the date that this Order is filed with the Chief Clerk of the

Commission’s Records Management Bureau or the Chief Clerk’s designee.

       SIGNED under the Seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, this 23rd day of

April, 2026.
